analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/reference/configuration.md line 410, the DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK row. It adds ClusterServiceCommand.swift (`supervisorConfiguration`) as a reader and says the variable also skips the `darkbloom cluster` pair's update at its slot. No code changes appear in the supplied evidence. I examined the two supplied head_text excerpts (lines 484-944). They are unchanged context and cover the MiMo, Flash-Next, DiffusionGemma, Bonsai, memory, hashing, prompt cache, SSD prefix cache, cluster and runtime-facts config tables. The excerpts show no changes to security controls, and I found no regression against the threat model.

One point for integration: line 410 documents that DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK now also suppresses the cluster pair's update. That variable already skips the in-daemon auto-update and the watchdog update check. It is an operator-local environment variable, not remotely settable. Any provider-process environment control stays inside the local operator's trust (TB-003, ADV-001). I cannot confirm from the supplied evidence that the cluster supervisor actually behaves as documented. The patch excerpt is also truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so the claim is unverified against ClusterServiceCommand.swift. If the code change is in the same PR, a reviewer should check whether it creates an update-suppression or downgrade path for cluster members (T-043, T-047 analogues). That is a question about code outside this batch, not a finding.

Prefix-cache rows (T-041) and cache storage rows are context only. They match the threat model's 30-minute TTL and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill-switch, with no contradiction visible.
